findings.title: Queued fixture invocation does not recheck the absolute monotonic deadline
findings.trigger: Already queued microtask work advances the injected/default monotonic clock after the scheduler's snapshot but before its queued task continuation. No timer callback or abort event has executed.
findings.source_fact: boundedCall accepts a numeric remaining snapshot. Its Promise.resolve().then checks only settled before task(controller.signal); it has no fresh observe/deadline check. collectFixture snapshots before constructing/scheduling the request.
static_trace: Item starts at monotonic0 with deadline30000. Pending capture and implementation/file verification succeed.
A trusted IO hook queues microtask M during acknowledged pending/readback/verification. M will set a fixture monotonic tick to30001; it has not run yet.
Scheduler observes tick0, calls boundedCall with remaining30000, installs the timeout, and queues task microtask T behind M.
collectFixture awaits. FIFO microtasks execute M before T, so tick is now30001 while settled is stillfalse. T invokes the transport anyway because it tests only settled.
A promptly resolved fixture can win before a timer callback. Later post-terminal checks record an abort/overrun, but the late invocation has already occurred.
findings.impact: The collector can begin a fixture attempt after the bound absolute deadline. This concerns admission after earlier work finishes, not forcibly preempting a synchronous trusted callback; documenting non-preemption does not supply the missing admission check.
findings.minimal_correction: Pass a frozen absolute deadline plus the caller observe function (or an equivalent fresh admission predicate) into boundedCall and check current monotonic availability/deadline and abort inside the queued continuation immediately before task invocation. Preserve explicit timeout/aborted terminal and no follow-up semantics; do not introduce a new product/helper scope.
findings.bounded_regression_proposal: Private synthetic IO hook queues one queueMicrotask that advances a deterministic tick beyond the item deadline before the queued transport. Assert transport_calls0, no raw response/known usage, explicit aborted/timeout/pending outcome as defined, and read-only recovery. No real sleep, busy loop, provider or resource call required.

findings.trigger: Closed fixture with packets=null has six metadata files: baseline/questions/accounting/configuration/policy/manifest. A contiguous otherwise valid513event chain is below32MiB.
findings.source_fact: recoverFixture checks total names.length > MAX_EVENTS+7, then iterates all eventNames without an independent MAX_EVENTS check. Journal.emit refuses512+ on creation, but recovery does not use emit.

eventNames contains513; the loop reads, binds and replays all513 if the original inputs/chain/transitions/aggregate bytes are valid.

findings.impact: Recovery's declared finite event contract differs from creation by one event when packets are absent. No unbounded resource claim or provider/model outcome is inferred.
findings.minimal_correction: Independently refuse eventNames.length > MAX_EVENTS before reading any event, while retaining total file-count/aggregate-byte/name/chain checks.
findings.bounded_regression_proposal: Use a bounded private recovery fixture/facade exposing six expected metadata names and513 contiguous event names. Assert the specific event-count refusal before event file reads, without512 live transport calls or a large-data experiment. Cover512 admissible count separately under valid retained fixtures as appropriate.
